claims.text: The initial material consists of near-equiatomic, single-phase solid-solution nanoparticles containing five or more metals.
Sub-nanometric high-entropy-alloy clusters can be formed on CeO2 nanorods.
Introducing a sub-nanometric HEA cluster on CeO2 is an applicable intervention for pre-existing near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles of unspecified composition.
The intervention could overcome structural or chemical instability during catalytic operation.
The proposed stabilization applies throughout 773–1173 K.
Readily reducible CeO2 facets produce a pronounced hydrogen-spillover effect that aids formation of the HEA sub-nanoclusters.
Hydrogen spillover preserves the structural or chemical stability of the HEA particles during operation.
Multielement mixing occurs in quantum-sized regions of the sub-nanometric HEA clusters.
Multielement mixing in quantum-sized regions preserves stability in the 773–1173 K regime.
CeO2-supported CoNiCuZnPd sub-nanoclusters have higher activity for NO reduction by H2 than the corresponding monometallic catalysts.
The sub-nanometric clusters exhibit structural reversibility under repeated oxidative and reductive exposure.
The reported structural reversibility demonstrates prolonged thermal stability at 773–1173 K.
Catalytic activity and structural stability would be measured over time during thermal exposure.
XANES would be used to monitor the oxidation states of the non-noble metals.

contradictions.description: The initial material is a five-or-more-metal solid-solution nanoparticle, but the stated baseline and supported activity comparison are monometallic catalysts rather than the same multimetallic nanoparticles without the intervention.
